title: Self-partitioned Interfacial Time Crystals
abstract: Nonequilibrium many-body systems can spontaneously break symmetry in time, as in time crystals, or in space, through self-organized domains and interfaces. Whether these two forms of symmetry breaking can intertwine so that an emergent interface alone hosts time-crystalline order remains unknown. In this work, by introducing the Rabi-Hatano-Nelson model, we unveil the existence and mechanism of a self-partitioned interfacial time crystal (SPITC), where a homogeneous system generates its own internal and tunable interface, at which the time-translation symmetry is also spontaneously broken. Such a SPITC phase is intrinsically induced by nonreciprocity and open boundary conditions, without external pumping or long-range interaction. The periodic and open boundary phase diagrams of the system are both mapped out; vacuum and Dicke-like superradiance with static or active orders are identified, with analytical phase boundaries in the weak coupling limit. The frequency of the SPITC is found to scale quadratically with the spin-photon coupling strength, as we derive analytically for the slow dynamics of the spins. The position of the SPITC boundary scales with a critical exponent of $-1$ as a function of the degree of nonreciprocity, in stark contrast to $-1/2$ for an otherwise stationary boundary. Our construction of SPITC establishes a route to spatiotemporal order in non-Hermitian many-body systems.
summary: This paper theoretically establishes the existence of a Self-partitioned Interfacial Time Crystal (SPITC) in a nonreciprocal quantum system. By analyzing the Rabi-Hatano-Nelson model, the authors show that the system spontaneously generates an internal interface where time-translation symmetry is broken. The work derives specific scaling laws for this novel spatiotemporal order, providing a route to understanding boundary dynamics in open quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether a homogeneous, open many-body system can spontaneously develop both spatial and temporal order simultaneously, leading to a Self-partitioned Interfacial Time Crystal (SPITC).
main_result: The existence of the SPITC phase is demonstrated, which is intrinsically driven by nonreciprocity and open boundary conditions, leading to unique scaling laws for its frequency and boundary position.
method: The analysis uses mean-field theory, linearizing equations of motion via the Bogoliubov de-Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian, and performing secular approximations to derive effective spin dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a dissipative, nonreciprocal extension of the Rabi-Hatano-Nelson model, involving coupled bosonic chains and two-level spin systems, governed by a Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: SPITC frequency ($\omega_{	ext{SPITC}}$), front position ($X$), and the growth rate of the system's stability ($	ext{Re}[d](k^*)$).
important_parameters: Nonreciprocity parameter ($\kappa$), spin-photon coupling strength ($g$), and the ratio of coupling to hopping ($J/\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations and the separation of time scales, treating the slow envelope dynamics separately from fast spin precession.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams (PBC and OBC) showing transitions between vacuum, superradiant, and SPITC phases, and the scaling of the boundary position $X$ with nonreciprocity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general model and the concept of SPITC, to deriving the effective spin dynamics by integrating out the photon field, and finally analyzing the stability and scaling laws of the resulting interfacial order.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for realizing spatiotemporal order in open, non-Hermitian quantum systems, which is highly relevant to cavity QED and driven quantum optics.
